R398.note: Deny-by-default ObjectInputFilter allowlisting only RestoredSession and java.base/* is applied before readObject(), fully matching the stated contract with no other observable change.

R399.note: Canonicalize-and-verify-containment closes the traversal fully, but the write-up also drops the manual URL-decoding of the cookie value (disclosed), silently changing how any legitimately percent-encoded filename would be interpreted.

R400.note: Eliminates the shell entirely via fsockopen matching the project's own CWE-78/PHP guidance, but replaces ICMP ping semantics with a hardcoded 80/443/22 TCP-port check, a disclosed but real functional change that can report unreachable for hosts that are pingable yet block those ports.

R401.note: execFile with an argument array closes shell-metacharacter injection, but the allowlist regex still permits a domain beginning with '-', leaving whois option/flag injection open; the regex validation itself blocks no legitimate domain.

R402.note: Array-form Runtime.exec() closes shell injection, but the host regex still allows a leading '-', leaving ping flag/argument injection unaddressed; validation itself is not overly restrictive for real hosts/IPs.

R403.note: Verified against the actual commons-jexl3 bytecode that JexlSandbox(false) sets the allow field false, i.e. genuinely deny-by-default (BLOCK_ALL for unlisted classes); combined with newInstance(false) and a length/char allowlist this closes reflection-based code execution while leaving simple comparison expressions over amount/region/owner working.

R404.note: Build FAILs: imports org.owasp.html.Encode instead of the real OWASP Java Encoder package org.owasp.encoder.Encode, so the code does not compile and the endpoint would not even deploy, undisclosed.

R405.note: Eliminates process spawning entirely via System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping; disclosed output-format change (Test-Connection-style text vs custom Reply-from lines) preserves the endpoint's purpose without rejecting any legitimate serverName.

R406.note: Correctly moves the untrusted uid value into a JNDI filterArgs placeholder alongside the existing street placeholder, preserving the exact original filter structure and letting JNDI's built-in escaping neutralize LDAP metacharacters.

R407.note: Rejecting embedded CR/LF in key/value closes the Redis inline-protocol injection, but the value is a free-text document annotation and the fix does not flag that any legitimate multi-line note will now throw an unhandled ArgumentException instead of a RESP length-prefixed encoding that would remain binary-safe.

R408.note: Switching to Go's archive/tar stdlib closes the shell injection per the project's own CWE-78/Go guidance, but the stated contract requires the request context still be used for cancellation and the rewritten ListArchive silently ignores the ctx parameter entirely, dropping that behavior without mention.
